reason: The artifact provides no test.py/get_inputs, so problem.txt is the operative contract. It explicitly requires result[s,t] = kv_cache[block_table[s, t//page_size], t % page_size], states that "the physical pages of one sequence are not contiguous and are generally interleaved with those of other sequences," and widens the input domain with "the block table may map any sequence to any physical page." Claim c1 is confirmed and in_scope with scope evidence citing exactly that stated domain: kernel.py passes BlockTable as an argument but never dereferences it; line 15 synthesizes physical = seq*max_blocks + logical_block, hardcoding an identity/contiguous page allocation. Probe t8 shows the signature of that defect under bit-exact equality (the correct metric for a pure data-movement gather, no precision or reduction-order excuse applies): with num_pages = num_seqs*max_blocks = 32 so no out-of-bounds confound, the contiguous/identity table matches exactly (0/512 and 0/400 tokens wrong), while a random permutation block table — an input the contract explicitly admits — yields 496/512 (96.9%) wrong tokens at seq_len=128 and 384/400 (96.0%) at seq_len=100, max abs err 6.28. The reference is well-defined and finite in these cases, so this is a genuine violation of a behavior the contract explicitly requires, not a tie-break, layout-convention, or tolerance artifact. Claim c2 (unmasked/unclamped index reading past kv_cache when num_pages < num_seqs*max_blocks) remains formally inconclusive in the ledger; the follow-up probe t12 supports the mechanism (all 256 tokens with synthesized index >= num_pages matched backing memory beyond kv_cache's extent, and a far-out-of-range configuration raised a CUDA illegal memory access), but I am setting c2 aside as a corollary of the same root cause because it is not needed for the verdict. c1 alone is sufficient.
